correctness.rationale: For d>=3 and R>1, the full planar meridian projection is the convex stadium [-R,R]×{0}+D2. Each transverse radial fiber is an interval; the meridian disk meets the rotation axis in j=0,1,2 intervals corresponding to j meridian circle-disks hit by the slicing line. Rotating yields S^{d−3}×D², D^{d−1}, S^{d−2}×I. The exact conditional normal/offset measures yield the three formulas. N(R)=E min(RX,1) has N″=−f_X(1/R)/R³<0, so the derivative numerator decreases and changes sign once. Comparing the optimum to the R→1+ limit gives R_d≤mu_d^−2. The high-dimensional Gaussian projection and uniform-integrability argument give the compact-uniform limiting deficit; F′=2Phi(sqrt(2lambda))−3/2 has one zero and F_min=q phi(q). Fresh standalone checker passed 106 finite assertions, including exact d3 formula regression and independent weighted sampling; numerical checks are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The question of how rotational toroidal topologies survive affine sectioning has concrete mathematical motivation from recently constructed S1×S^{n−1} embedded rotational hypersurfaces. The generic section topology changes sharply from disconnected sections at d=3 to connected ones at d=4 and simply connected at d>=5; an exact natural probability law and unique shape optimizer are complete in all d. Its high-dimensional optimum lies at a sharp d^-1 distance from the horn boundary with a nontrivial normal-quantile constant; this is a structural geometric-probability phenomenon rather than a renamed classical 3D result. The work explicitly does not assert that the particular f-minimal tori or all toroidal embeddings obey the formulas.
